title: Managing Services with Compose CLI knowledge check

questions.prompt: Which statement best captures the central idea of “Managing Services with Compose CLI”?
options: Describe related services and resources in compose.yaml, then validate the resolved configuration.
Use Compose only to build one executable source file.
Assume depends_on always means a dependency is ready to accept traffic.
Put each container on a separate, unconnected network by default.
questions.answer_key: Describe related services and resources in compose.yaml, then validate the resolved configuration.
questions.explanation: Compose is declarative and can manage services, networks, volumes and configuration; readiness still needs health/retry behavior.

questions.prompt: For a lab covering managing services with compose cli, what is the strongest evidence of learning?
options: Assume the command is portable and skip reading its output.
Make several unrelated changes before collecting a baseline.
Use a production host so the result looks realistic.
Record the command or configuration, predicted result, observed evidence, and one relevant edge case.
questions.answer_key: Record the command or configuration, predicted result, observed evidence, and one relevant edge case.
questions.explanation: A useful lab connects a predicted result to actual output and checks an edge case. This is safer and more reproducible than assuming success.

questions.prompt: If an example related to managing services with compose cli fails, which response is best?
options: Disable permissions or security controls until the example works.
Trust the image tag without inspecting the image or version.
Reproduce the issue, inspect state/logs/configuration, test one hypothesis at a time, and verify the fix.
Delete every stopped container and unused volume before investigating.
questions.answer_key: Reproduce the issue, inspect state/logs/configuration, test one hypothesis at a time, and verify the fix.
questions.explanation: The evidence-led approach keeps the diagnosis reproducible and avoids hiding the cause. For managing services with compose cli, verify the fix with the exact setting or command that failed.
